methods.label: Locate the roots and bound every edge
methods.explanation:
A lower bound for every possible edge will give a lower bound for every polygon's perimeter. We first locate all eight roots.

Let \(q=2+\sqrt3\), so \(q^2=7+4\sqrt3\). The polynomial factors as
\[
P(z)=(z^4-1)(z^4+q^2).
\]
The equation \(z^4=1\) gives \(z=1,-1,i,-i\), corresponding to the four points \((\pm1,0)\) and \((0,\pm1)\).

For the other factor,
\[
z^4+q^2=(z^2-iq)(z^2+iq),
\]
so \(z^2=iq\) or \(z^2=-iq\). Set \(a=(1+\sqrt3)/2\); then \(2a^2=q\), and
\[
(a+ai)^2=iq,\qquad (a-ai)^2=-iq.
\]
Taking both square roots in each case gives the four points \((\pm a,\pm a)\), with the signs chosen independently. The factorizations account for all roots, and these eight points are distinct because \(a>1\).

Now compare all types of pairs. Among the four axis points, the smallest distance is \(\sqrt2\). Among the four corner points \((\pm a,\pm a)\), the smallest distance is \(2a>\sqrt2\). For an axis point and a corner point, symmetry reduces the squared distance to one of
\[
a^2+(a-1)^2=2
\quad\text{or}\quad
a^2+(a+1)^2>2.
\]
Thus every edge joining distinct roots has length at least \(\sqrt2\). Any eight-sided polygon using the roots therefore has perimeter at least \(8\sqrt2\).

To attain the bound, join the points in their order around the origin, alternating axis points and corner points. Every consecutive pair is a nearest axis-corner pair, so all eight edges have length \(\sqrt2\). Each edge stays in the \(45^\circ\) sector between its endpoint rays, so nonadjacent edges do not cross. This is a valid eight-sided polygon attaining the bound.

The minimum perimeter is \(\boxed{8\sqrt2}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
